body:
Java and FTC foundation lessons. Applicability is limited to FTC SDK 11.1.0 and Java 8 source syntax; this is not production support certification. Original explanations and examples use this repository's MIT license. Upstream references retain their own notices and terms; upstream documentation and sample programs are not reproduced here. Replace placeholders only with actual Driver Station configuration. A successful build does not prove robot behavior.

References: [FTC SDK 11.1 sample source](https://github.com/FIRST-Tech-Challenge/FtcRobotController/tree/203c2d373765f0c66d121e3ec1cc3a18835f6534/FtcRobotController/src/main/java/org/firstinspires/ftc/robotcontroller/external/samples), [RobotCore 11.1.0 sources](https://repo.maven.apache.org/maven2/org/firstinspires/ftc/RobotCore/11.1.0/RobotCore-11.1.0-sources.jar), [Java SE 8 types](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/specs/jls/se8/html/jls-4.html), [packages](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/specs/jls/se8/html/jls-7.html), [classes and methods](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/specs/jls/se8/html/jls-8.html), [statements](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/specs/jls/se8/html/jls-14.html), [expressions](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/specs/jls/se8/html/jls-15.html).

lessons.title: Java values, decisions and methods

exercises.prompt: Predict the helper results, then apply the same typed input calculation in your own project without commanding an actuator.
exercises.explanationCriteria: Explain parameter and return types, assignment versus comparison, the branch result and why changing the sign does not prove a physical direction.
exercises.projectApplicationCriteria: Add or adapt a named calculation in your existing TeamCode project; provide the actual file and call site, a table of predicted inputs/results and an explanation of where fresh input is read. Record compilation separately from any later robot observation.

lessons.title: From INIT to STOP

exercises.prompt: Annotate lifecycle boundaries and adapt the observational OpMode to an existing project.
exercises.explanationCriteria: Explain which statements run before START, why the post-wait stop check exists, and how a linear loop differs from iterative callbacks.
exercises.projectApplicationCriteria: Provide the actual project file with setup, wait and stop-aware repetition identified. Write expected INIT/START/STOP observations; label them predicted until a deliberately authorized supervised run records what actually happened. A build alone does not complete that observation.

lessons.title: Map hardware and observe inputs

exercises.prompt: Adapt the mapping placeholder and plan an input/telemetry observation for your project.
exercises.explanationCriteria: Explain the type/name lookup, when gamepad fields are reread, encoder counts versus physical distance, and why telemetry delivery is not guaranteed each iteration.
exercises.projectApplicationCriteria: Use only your actual configured motor name and type; identify their configuration evidence and the Java call site. Provide expected stick/button/encoder observations without inventing readings. If supervised hardware testing is unavailable, mark actual observations not run and keep the placeholder visible until the real name is known.

lessons.title: Make code explainable

exercises.prompt: Connect the helper to an observational OpMode and explain the responsibility of each file.
exercises.explanationCriteria: Explain package/file/class correspondence, parameters and the return value, and why the helper computes a request while the OpMode owns lifecycle and input reads.
exercises.projectApplicationCriteria: Show the actual helper file and active-loop call site in your project, preserve existing team files, and trace one predicted input to the displayed request. Include a brief code walkthrough; compile evidence and supervised robot observations must be labelled separately.
